SPECS Specs PHOTOS Photos Product Description Iconic 60s fuzz, reborn for modern players . Few effects have defined the sound of electric guitar quite like fuzz. The VFZ-1 celebrates this legacy by revisiting one of the most influential fuzz circuits of all time: the classic two-transistor of the late 60s commonly known as the Mk 1.5, whose expressive breakup inspired a generation of players. Classic Germanium character; Modern Silicon stability Vintage fuzz boxes are beloved for their warm, harmonically rich distortion, but their Germanium transistors present familiar issues: temperature drift, inconsistent performance, and high noise. While Silicon solves these problems, it rarely recreates the musical sweetness of Germanium, until now. After extensive analysis of prized vintage units, VOX engineers developed a Silicon-based design that retains the magic of those originals. Each of the two silicon transistors is biased at a precisely calculated operating point, allowing them to interact in the same musical, interdependent way as the best Mk 1.5 circuits. The result is a fuzz that is aggressive yet refined, dynamic yet stable, combining timeless tone with modern reliability and exceptionally low noise. Key Features Vintage two-transistor fuzz design updated with modern stability Silicon transistors voiced for authentic Germanium-like tone and response Precisely targeted biasing for an expanded sweet spot and natural cleanup Two premium silicon transistors Crunch Switch for lower-gain, volume-rolled-back overdrive tones Bass Cut and Tone Cut controls for wide-ranging tonal shaping High input impedance allows placement anywhere in your signal chain—even after Wah pedals or buffers Exceptionally low noise performance Compact, rugged, vintage-style enclosure Modern 9V pedalboard-friendly power compatibility   read more The sound of classic fuzz and more The VFZ-1’s carefully biased first transistor offers unusually high input impedance for a vintage-style fuzz, preserving your guitar’s

Vox browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive fuzz browse by enclosure pedal events 2026 NAMM 2026 Vox VFZ-1 Fuzz - Classic Mk1.5 Fuzz Published on January 15, 2026 Vox fuzz pedal NAMM 2026 Information The Vox VFZ-1 is a compact fuzz effect pedal designed to recreate the expressive two-transistor fuzz tones of the late 1960s while addressing the limitations of vintage designs through modern engineering. Inspired by classic Mk 1.5-style fuzz circuits, the VFZ-1 employs a dual-transistor architecture built around two silver-can BC108 silicon transistors, voiced and biased to deliver a germanium-like response with improved stability, lower noise, and consistent performance. The circuit focuses on dynamic touch sensitivity, smooth compression, and rich overtone saturation, allowing the pedal to transition from aggressive fuzz to cleaner, volume-responsive textures with natural cleanup. A key design element of the VFZ-1 is its carefully biased first gain stage, which provides unusually high input impedance for a vintage-style fuzz. This preserves the guitar's natural harmonics and enables full compatibility with buffered pedals and wah effects, allowing flexible placement anywhere in the signal chain. The second transistor stage shapes the breakup character, recreating the smooth, valve-like compression and sustain associated with classic fuzz sounds. Together, the stages produce a mid-rich, musical fuzz character with enhanced control and usability compared to original late-1960s units. Beyond traditional fuzz controls, the VFZ-1 integrates expanded tone-shaping options for modern players. Dedicated Bass Cut and Tone Cut controls allow precise adjustment of low and high frequency content, enabling tighter low end for humbuckers or neck pickups and smoother high-frequency roll-off for classic violin-like sustain. A Crunch switch introduces a lower-gain mode that emulates the sound of rolling back the guitar's volume control, producing chime-like overdrive tones without adjusting the instrument itself. These features extend the pedal's range from full fuzz saturation to responsive low-gain textures. VOX VFZ-1 Fuzz Pedal Pro Gear Advisers Chat

- Inspired by classic Mk 1.5-style fuzz circuits, the VFZ-1 employs a dual-transistor architecture built around two silver-can BC108 silicon transistors, voiced and biased to deliver a germanium-like response with improved stability, lower noise, and consistent performance.
- This preserves the guitar's natural harmonics and enables full compatibility with buffered pedals and wah effects, allowing flexible placement anywhere in the signal chain.

Few effects have defined the sound of electric guitar quite like fuzz.
The VFZ-1 celebrates this legacy by revisiting one of the most influential fuzz circuits of all time: the classic two-transistor of the late 60s commonly known as the Mk 1.5, whose expressive breakup inspired a generation of players.
Classic Germanium character; Modern Silicon stability Vintage fuzz boxes are beloved for their warm, harmonically rich distortion, but their Germanium transistors present familiar issues: temperature drift, inconsistent performance, and high noise.
